# Vagueness of Words

With the vagueness of words,  
a secret unveils itself, but partly—  
like an image in a hazy mirror,  
a fragment of a greater whole;  

that through phrasing, like breath, must uncover  
meaning from the vast expanse of being,  
words that once drifted like feather-seeds on the wind,  
now must bind themselves to steadfast meaning—  

as in Mahākāsyapa’s silent laugh  
when he gazes at the flower in the Buddha’s hand,  
quietly conveying to those who lack the words:  
“the kingdom within you—there lies your inheritance.”
